Compare two NONMEM runs

Source: R/nm_compare.R, R/nm_compare_stats.R
nm_compare.Rd

Paired comparison of two NONMEM runs at the observation level (CWRES, NPDE) and at the subject level (individual OFV from .phi). Provides a summary of residual diagnostics, per-subject iOFV deltas, and identifies which subjects drive the OFV difference.

Usage

nm_compare(
  run1,
  run2,
  labels = c("Run 1", "Run 2"),
  join_keys = c("ID", "TIME"),
  n_par = NULL,
  nested = FALSE,
  covariates = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  n_boot = 2000L,
  seed = 2026L
)

# S3 method for class 'nm_compare'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'nm_compare'
summary(object, ...)

Arguments

run1, run2

Path to a run directory or run prefix (without extension). Each location must contain at least a sdtab* table. .phi and .lst files are used if available for iOFV and global OFV respectively.

labels

Character vector of length 2. Display labels for the two runs.

join_keys

Character vector. Columns used to pair observations between runs. Default c("ID", "TIME"). Add "OCC" for BOV models, "CMT" for multi-DV models.

n_par

Numbers of estimated parameters of the two runs (length 2). Default: read from the .ext files (parameters not fixed).

nested

TRUE if one model is nested in the other: a likelihood ratio test is added to the Vuong and Clarke tests.

covariates

Covariates (columns of the data set) against which the per-subject delta iOFV is examined.

data

Data set (path or data.frame) holding the covariates. Default: the $DATA file of run 1.

n_boot

Number of subject resamples for the bootstrap of the delta iOFV.

seed

Seed of the bootstrap.

x

An nm_compare object.

...

Unused.

object

An nm_compare object.

Value

An object of class nm_compare, a list with:

data_obs

Observation-level paired data.frame with _1/_2 suffixed columns and delta columns (dCWRES, dAbsCWRES, dNPDE, dAbsNPDE).

data_subj

Per-subject summary including iOFV_1, iOFV_2, diOFV, and residual aggregates.

metrics

Global metrics table (OFV, RMSE(CWRES), Mean |CWRES|, proportions of outliers, NPDE moments). Wilcoxon paired p-value stored as attribute wilcox_absCWRES_p.

meta

Labels, global OFV, numbers of parameters, sample sizes, dataset compatibility check.

tests

Vuong, Clarke (and LRT) tests, subject bootstrap and influence (NULL without .phi files).

parameters

Estimates, SE, RSE and shrinkage of the two runs matched by parameter name, with their ratio.

etas

Paired EBEs of the ETAs present in both runs.

covariate_tests

Delta iOFV versus each covariate.

run_info

Run-level criteria (RSE, condition number, shrinkage, status).

summary(): a data.frame of decision criteria (class nm_compare_summary), one row per criterion with the value for each run and the run it favours.

Details

Observations are merged on join_keys (default c("ID", "TIME")). If the two datasets differ (e.g. different BLQ handling), only the intersection is retained and a warning is issued.

Tests on the individual contributions. With d_i = (iOFV_1,i - iOFV_2,i)/2, the difference of the individual log-likelihoods, the Vuong (1989) statistic is z = (sum(d_i) - c) / (sqrt(N) * sd(d_i)) and the Clarke (2007) test is a sign test on d_i - c/N, where N is the number of subjects and c the correction for the number of parameters: none, k_2 - k_1 (AIC-like) or (k_2 - k_1) log(N) / 2 (BIC-like). Both apply to non-nested models fitted to the same data; the subjects are the independent units. The individual contributions are those of the estimation method (FOCE: the iOFV of the .phi file).

Bootstrap. The subjects are resampled with their delta iOFV, without re-estimation: the distribution measures how much the difference depends on a few subjects, conditionally on the estimates (optimistic for the larger model).

Influence. n_reverse is the number of subjects with the largest contributions whose removal reverses the sign of dOFV (as dOFV.vs.id in xpose4).

References

Vuong QH. Likelihood ratio tests for model selection and non-nested hypotheses. Econometrica 1989;57:307-33.

Clarke KA. A simple distribution-free test for nonnested model selection. Political Analysis 2007;15:347-63.

See also

nm_extract_runs(), plot.nm_compare(), print.nm_compare()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
  cmp <- nm_compare("runs/run42", "runs/run43",
                    labels = c("Base", "+ CLcr"))
  print(cmp)
  plot(cmp)
  plot(cmp, type = "iofv_caterpillar")
  summary(cmp)
  plot(cmp, type = c("gain_map", "overlay_gof"))
} # }
